Subject: Finova: follow-up + SLO matrix (post-call)

Hi Sophie / Miguel 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

1) Primary production use case: customer-facing chat assistant for mortgage eligibility and pre-qualification. Expectation is sub-second responses for interactive flows (streaming preferred).
2) Traffic profile (initial): 100 qps peak, average payload ~120 tokens per request. Expected growth: 3x in 12 months.
3) Latency targets discussed: regionally scoped p95 goals  want to confirm exact numbers below.
4) Concurrency/throughput: sustained concurrency target ~200 concurrent sessions; spikes to 400 for limited windows (end of month).
5) Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region; APAC customers similarly flagged for local residency in 2027.

Attached is a first-pass SLO matrix (Finova-SLO-matrix-v1.xlsx) with columns for region, p50/p95 targets, throughput, concurrency, and streaming vs non-streaming requirements. I highlighted where we need your confirmation (yellow cells).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the p95/p99 targets per region and whether streaming is mandatory for all endpoints or only a subset.
- If EU residency is strict for EU customers, confirm whether logs/analytics need to be stored in-region as well.
- I'll loop in Aditya to validate feasibility of the throughput and routing design and get a rough cost/architecture sketch.

Would Monday morning for a short 30-min follow-up work? I can share an updated SLO matrix after your replies.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Finova: follow-up + SLO matrix (post-call)

Marissa 

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Regional latency targets (p95, end-to-end response time to our frontend):
   US (primary region): 100ms p95 target for most interactive flows; 60ms p50.
   EU: 150ms p95 (we have customers in Germany/France with stricter UX expectations).
   APAC: 250ms p95 (acceptable for now, but we want to improve over time).

- Streaming: yes  streaming is required for the main chat flow (progressive tokens rendered to the user). Non-streaming OK for async batch reranking/embeddings.

- Throughput/concurrency: the 100 qps peak was a conservative estimate. Our product analytics team expects 150 qps within 6 months; concurrency estimate of 300 sustained, spikes to 600 during heavy campaigns (we'll provide historical traffic slices).

- Data residency: EU data must remain in the EU for storage and audit logs. We can route inference requests out of-region for latency but cannot replicate or persist user PII outside EU. For APAC, we prefer APAC residency for local users starting Q2 2027.

I've attached a short annotated version of your matrix with our edits (Finova-SLO-matrix-v1-annotated.xlsx).

If you can send an updated matrix reflecting the regional p95 numbers and an initial proposal for routing (primary region + fallback rules), we can review and set the follow-up call. Monday 09:30 PT works for Miguel and me.

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
VP Product Operations | Finova
sophie.turner@finova.com

Subject: Re: Finova: follow-up + SLO matrix (post-call)

Thanks Sophie  this is super helpful. I've updated the SLO matrix to reflect the p95 targets and concurrency numbers (see attached Finova-SLO-matrix-v2.xlsx). High-level proposal summary:

1) Regional routing model:
   - Primary routing by customer region header (US/EU/APAC).
   - If primary capacity is saturated, automatic fallback to nearest compatible region within policy (e.g., EU -> US fallback only for non-PII payloads).
   - For EU-resident PII, enforce in-region execution and in-region logging (no external replicas).

2) Serving profile & capacity:
   - Recommend Dedicated capacity for initial production (reserved pool per region) to guarantee throughput and p95 targets.
   - Autoscaling with cold-start smoothing + burst pool to handle 2x spikes.

3) Streaming & latency optimizations:
   - Use token streaming with continuous batching and KV-cache to keep p95 low.
   - For ultra-low latency endpoints, we can pin smaller decoder-only variants with quantization to meet 60100ms p95 in US.

4) Fallback & graceful degradation:
   - Canary smaller model variants for high-load periods; degrade feature-rich responses to short answers to preserve latency SLOs.

5) Data residency & audit logs:
   - EU: keep inference, logs, and analytics in EU region. We recommend Private control plane or Dedicated regional deployment with KMS integration for audit log retention in-region.

Next actions:
- Sophie/Miguel: confirm that EU PII prohibition on cross-region persistence is firm (yes/no).
- Finova: share sample traffic slice (1-hour trace) and example payload sizes for the chat endpoint.
- Redwood: Aditya and team will size Dedicated pools per-region and provide ballpark cost and baseline capacity plan by Wed EOD.

I'll see you on Monday 09:30 PT. Thanks again.

Best,
Marissa

marissa.cole@redwood.inference

Aditya / Dev 

Looping you in on the exchange with Finova. Key asks for engineering sizing:

- Targets to hit: US p95=100ms (p50=60ms), EU p95=150ms, APAC p95=250ms. Streaming required for chat.
- Traffic: current peak ~100150 qps, forecast to 300 qps within 6 months; concurrency sustained ~300, spikes to 600.
- Data residency: EU inference + logs must remain in-region; APAC residency required by Q2 2027.

Please confirm feasibility of:
1) Dedicated regional pools (US/EU/APAC) to meet p95 with continuous batching + streaming.
2) Fallback policy that allows EU -> US fallback for non-PII only; PII must never leave EU.
3) Quick back-of-envelope capacity/cost estimate per region (ballpark) so I can share with the customer ahead of next call.

Also flag any redlines / showstoppers. Finova is sensitive about cross-region logging and will likely require in-region KMS for EU.

Thanks  can you aim to have notes by Wed EOD? I'll incorporate into a short one-pager for Sophie.
